chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Abu Sa'id, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about deriving pleasure from the virgins who are between the parents (i.e., concubines/slaves owned jointly by husband and wife or parents), so he said, 'There is no harm, and I do not say as those Ashab say.'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعِ: Deriving pleasure (specifically sexual pleasure in this context)
key_terms.الْأَقْشَابُ: The Aqshab (a group of jurists or a specific school of thought)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on deriving pleasure from virgin slave girls owned jointly by the parents in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the permissibility of deriving sexual pleasure from virgin slave girls owned jointly by their masters, distinguishing his ruling from the 'Aqshab' (often identified as the Hanafis or a specific juristic group) who may have imposed stricter conditions. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view on the rights of owners over their female slaves, emphasizing that joint ownership does not invalidate the permissibility of *tamattu'* for the owners. The reference to 'Aqshab' serves to contextualize the hadith within early Islamic debates on marriage and concubinage laws.
